description:
Advances: ancora.review

Severity: Medium (calibrated). Follow-up from the /ship-it critical review (consolidated finding F16) and from the ancora-ayj cold verify.

Problem: the spec.review artifact embeds each changed file complete diff once per affected subject PLUS once under All files. Measured on this branch: 1105 diff articles for 175 distinct files, exactly 8 copies each, 9.65 MB, 301,143 DOM nodes, 5 second reload. Mechanism is lib/ancora/review.ex:137-143, where supporting is derived from the GLOBAL changed_files list for every subject, filtered only by source_file?/1, never consulting that subject derived footprint.

Why this ticket is needed now: F16 used to be a contract violation with a citable line, because ancora.review.code_pivot_grouping said clause-level hunk. Ticket ancora-ayj correctly rewrote that line to describe what the code actually does (there is no hunk-slicing anywhere in the module, so the old wording described something never built). That was the honest fix and it is merged. The side effect is that F16 lost its written basis, and nothing replaces it: ancora.review.size_budget bounds renderer SOURCE lines (5,000 across lib/ancora/review/ plus lib/ancora/markdown.ex), not artifact bytes. Today the artifact could reach 50 MB and the gate would stay green.

Deliverable, recommended verbatim by the cold verifier: add a must to ancora.review alongside size_budget that bounds the rendered ARTIFACT rather than the renderer source. Suggested wording: the rendered artifact shall include each changed file diff at most twice (once under the subject that owns it, once under All files), and shall stay under N MB for a change set of 200 files, enforced by a standing test. Pair it with a scenario building a multi-subject fixture that asserts the per-file article count, so the test FAILS today and passes once supporting changes are scoped to the owning subject. Note size_budget own cut list already names the right lever (supporting-changes hunks degrade to a file-link list); it was simply wired to the source-line budget instead of an artifact budget.

Knock-on already observed: every id=file- exists 8 times, so the watched-card defining-file link resolves to a copy inside a display:none pivot and the page does not move when clicked (consolidated finding F38, same ticket).

Cannot land on the epic branch: this needs a new must plus a failing-then-passing standing test and a behavior change to subject scoping, which is a contract decision beyond the scope of the blocker fixes the ship was waiting on.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: a new standing test in test/ancora/review_test.exs (or test/ancora/static/review_budget_test.exs) building a multi-subject fixture and asserting the per-file diff article count and unique id=file- anchors, tagged to the new ancora.review requirement; existing tagged tests under ancora.review
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) new must in ancora.review next to size_budget bounding the rendered ARTIFACT: each changed file's diff appears at most twice (owning subject plus All files) and a 200-file change set stays under the stated MB ceiling; (2) the new test FAILS on the pre-change code (prove it in the IMPLEMENTED comment) and passes after supporting changes are scoped to the owning subject's derived footprint; (3) every id=file- anchor is unique so the watched-card defining-file link scrolls the page (F38)
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: each changed file's diff appears at most twice in the artifact, every file anchor is unique, and watched-card bindings come from the AST resolver against a written contract line.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/review.ex (supporting derived from the subject's footprint, not the global changed_files list)
- lib/ancora/review.ex binding extraction (F17: replace the regex with calls into lib/ancora/derive/resolver.ex; the resolver itself is read-only here)
- lib/ancora/review/html.ex (anchor uniqueness only; rendering defects belong to ancora-xla.4)
- lib/ancora/review/file_diff.ex
- test/ancora/review_test.exs, test/ancora/static/review_budget_test.exs, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md (new must plus scenario; substantive)
- .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.review_artifact_contract.md (only if the recorded boundary changes)

- .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator. This list already permits lib/ancora/derive/resolver.ex, which ancora.derive governs, so any edit there raises drift that only a substantive edit to this spec can clear. Acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement or scenario updates that clear drift, growth or shrink caused by THIS ticket's own changes. Never weaken a must, never delete a requirement.)
- Any spec whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false, for the sole purpose of correcting that statement in the same diff. Recorded after ancora-v1n shipped a corpus holding two scenarios that predicted opposite outcomes from identical input, because the spec stating the old rule was withheld from its Allowed list and the worker retagged around the conflict instead of flagging it. If you find a requirement anywhere in .spec/ that your change falsifies, fixing it here is in scope and expected. Say so in your completion record.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/derive/**
- lib/ancora/gate*
- lib/mix/tasks/**
- priv/spec_review_assets/**

Out of Scope (intent):
- no hunk slicing; the contract line ancora-ayj rewrote stays honest
- no Prism, badge, severity, or ARIA fixes here (ancora-xla.4)
- the extractor swap (F17, moved here from ancora-xla.9 by ruling) lands AFTER the contract line, in the same diff, with a before/after card diff on the existing fixtures

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission ends result=pass
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

comments.text: RULING (Manuel, 2026-09-03): F17 from ancora-xla.9 moves into this ticket. Write the new artifact-size must and the watched-card contract line first, then swap Ancora.Review's regex binding extractor for the AST resolver in the same diff, so the swap is tested against the contract you just wrote. Guard: before the swap lands, diff the watched-card output for the existing fixtures against the regex version and account for every difference in the IMPLEMENTED comment; the AST version must not silently drop bindings the regex found. Allowed touches now include lib/ancora/review.ex for the extractor and read access to lib/ancora/derive/resolver.ex (call it, do not edit it). The 'no regex-to-AST extractor swap here' line in Out of Scope (intent) is withdrawn. This ticket no longer blocks ancora-xla.9.

IMPLEMENTED

Tests added: Ancora.ReviewTest "production builder scopes file diffs to their subject and renders one file anchor"; Ancora.Static.ReviewBudgetTest "a 200-file review artifact stays below one megabyte"
Spec acknowledgment: .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md adds the substantive artifact-size must, unique watched-link contract, and two scenarios; .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.review_artifact_contract.md records the built footprint, anchor, and byte-budget boundary. No Spec-Ack trailer used.
Verification tier: change-scoped — mix compile --warnings-as-errors; mix test test/ancora/review_test.exs test/ancora/static/review_budget_test.exs; mix test --stale; mix format --check-formatted; mix deps.unlock --check-unused; mix spec.check --base b717ba4; full-system proof deferred to the merge gate / PR CI
Final-tier runs: 1

Summary: Review now uses the existing AST derive pipeline for watched bindings, limits supporting and test diffs to one deterministic subject owner, and emits each file anchor only in All files. Against the b717ba4 implementation, the fixture's watched cards changed from %{alpha: [], beta: [Fixture.Beta.next/1]} to %{alpha: [Fixture.Alpha.next/1], beta: [Fixture.Beta.next/1]}; the AST resolver added the aliased Alpha call and retained every regex-found binding. I checked every epic lesson against the diff: the defining "one" clause has a shared-footprint test, the before/after names both compared trees, the spec and decision match the code, the real Review.build/2 path reaches the behavior without seams, the rendered output proves the anchors and diff counts, and the regex extractor was deleted without adding a process, registry, or cache.

title: Re-base the review artifact size finding on a contract line that still exists
